If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecasted price by 1–2% in late horizon (last 7–14 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecasted price by 1–2% in mid horizon (days 10–20) to counteract downward bias.

If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative within 5 days, shift forecast downward by 1–3% in early horizon (first 5 days) to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) across 5+ consecutive days, apply a 0.5–1% upward bias in late horizon to compensate for lack of momentum.

If forecast consistently overestimates true price by >5% in early horizon, reduce forecast by 1–2% in mid horizon to correct for early overconfidence.

If forecast consistently underestimates true price by >5% in late horizon, increase forecast by 1–2% in mid horizon to align with actual breakout momentum.
